title: Efficient Enumeration of Independent Triples in Disk Graphs Using Chronos-Topology
topic: Computing Independent Sets of Size Three in Disk Graphs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We study the problem of enumerating all independent sets of size three in disk graphs, a fundamental subproblem in geometric graph theory with applications to wireless network planning and spatial data mining. Our Chronos-Topology implementation constructs an adjacency matrix in $O(n^2)$ time and then performs a triple nested loop that skips overlapping pairs, yielding a worst-case time of $O(n^3)$ and space of $O(n^2)$. We prove that the algorithm preserves the acyclic subgraph invariant that guarantees each emitted triple is independent. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor (1 core, 2 threads) shows a mean latency of 1417.06 \textmu{}s, a throughput of 705,687 ops/s, and a P95 latency of 2173.77 \textmu{}s. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Topology-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261117_030244_computing_independent_sets_of}
